interim_updates.note_text: Lanka Aluminium Industries PLC (LALU) reported a sharp YoY profit decline for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), driven by margin compression rather than a revenue collapse. Group revenue fell just 6% YoY to Rs.804.4mn (2025: Rs.851.8mn), but cost of sales rose 1% to Rs.669.5mn (2025: Rs.661.9mn) despite the lower volumes, pushing gross profit down 29% to Rs.134.9mn (2025: Rs.189.9mn) and gross margin down from 22.3% to 16.8%. Operating costs added further pressure: administrative expenses rose 13% to Rs.52.2mn (2025: Rs.46.3mn) and marketing and distribution expenses rose 19% to Rs.51.6mn (2025: Rs.43.4mn), so Group profit from operations fell 61% to Rs.39.5mn (2025: Rs.102.0mn). Net finance income partly offset this, rising 28% to Rs.11.7mn (2025: Rs.9.2mn) as finance income grew 27% to Rs.13.0mn while finance cost grew a similar 20% to Rs.1.2mn, leaving Group PBT down 54% to Rs.51.2mn (2025: Rs.111.2mn) and effective tax rate broadly stable (29.6% of PBT vs 29.9% a year ago). Final Group PAT fell 55% to Rs.35.1mn (2025: Rs.77.9mn), and profit attributable to equity holders of the company fell 51% to Rs.30.9mn (2025: Rs.63.7mn) -- the Group figure includes a small new -Rs.0.9mn post-tax share of loss from Comark Engineers (Pvt) Ltd's newly-acquired (Feb 2026) 28.07% stake in Equity Investments Lanka Limited, its first associate under the equity method, which did not materially change the outcome. Company (standalone) figures tell the same story: revenue actually grew 3% to Rs.762.4mn, but cost of sales grew faster at 8% to Rs.638.9mn, so gross profit fell 17% to Rs.123.5mn and gross margin fell from 20.0% to 16.2%; Company PBT fell 44% and PAT fell 43%. No segmental breakdown is disclosed in this filing (single reportable segment), so the specific product/customer mix behind the cost-of-sales increase cannot be isolated from the figures given.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for LALU -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. No segmental note is disclosed in this filing, so the driver behind the cost-of-sales increase (input cost vs mix vs pricing) cannot be isolated and is flagged qualitatively only. short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings reflect only the disclosed bank overdraft and are 0 where the filing shows a dash/no loans line -- not a missing-data gap, genuinely near-zero leverage.
interim_updates.takeaway: The headline PAT decline (-55% Group, -43% Company) is a margin story, not a demand collapse: revenue fell only 6% (Group) or grew 3% (Company), but cost of sales rose in both cases even as volumes softened, compressing gross margin from roughly 22% to 17% (Group) and 20% to 16% (Company) -- worth watching whether this is input-cost inflation (aluminium/energy) or pricing pressure, since the filing gives no segmental or cost-driver detail to distinguish the two. The company remains very lightly levered (Group short-term borrowings of only Rs.449k, no long-term debt), so the profit decline is not a balance-sheet risk in this quarter.

yoy.label: Profit for the period (Group, incl. NCI and associate share)

operational_highlights: Group revenue -6% YoY to Rs.804.4mn (2025: Rs.851.8mn); gross profit -29% to Rs.134.9mn as cost of sales rose 1% despite lower revenue -- gross margin fell from 22.3% to 16.8%.
Group profit from operations -61% YoY to Rs.39.5mn (2025: Rs.102.0mn) on the margin compression plus administrative expenses +13% and marketing/distribution expenses +19%.
Group PBT -54% YoY to Rs.51.2mn; Group PAT -55% YoY to Rs.35.1mn; profit attributable to equity holders -51% YoY to Rs.30.9mn (2025: Rs.63.7mn).
Company (standalone) revenue actually grew 3% YoY to Rs.762.4mn, but cost of sales grew faster (+8%), so Company gross margin still fell from 20.0% to 16.2% and Company PAT fell 43%.

Balance sheet remains very lightly geared: Group short-term borrowings of only Rs.449k (bank overdraft) and zero long-term borrowings; net asset value per share rose to Rs.45.25 (31.03.2026: Rs.44.80).

First-ever associate investment: Comark Engineers (Pvt) Ltd (a subsidiary) acquired a 28.07% stake in Equity Investments Lanka Limited in Feb 2026, contributing a small -Rs.0.9mn post-tax share of loss this quarter.
key_drivers: Cost of sales rose YoY (Group +1% to Rs.669.5mn, Company +8% to Rs.638.9mn) even as Group revenue fell 6% -- the primary driver of the gross margin compression from roughly 22% to 17%/16%; the filing discloses no segmental note to identify whether this is raw material (aluminium) cost inflation or a product/customer mix shift.

Administrative expenses +13% (Group, Rs.52.2mn vs Rs.46.3mn) and marketing/distribution expenses +19% (Group, Rs.51.6mn vs Rs.43.4mn) compounded the gross margin hit, turning a 29% gross profit decline into a 61% operating profit decline.
Net finance income improved 28% YoY (Rs.11.7mn vs Rs.9.2mn Group), a genuine partial offset, but too small relative to the Rs.62.5mn drop in operating profit to change the overall direction.
